Below is the complete 12-week programme summary you requested — integrated: upper‑body strength (rehab‑aware), rotator cuff/scapular work, hangboard and climbing prep, two weekly cardio sessions, mobility, nutrition for body recomposition, and a Saturday fun full‑body finisher. It assumes her physio has cleared progression steps, and all work is pain‑free (stop and regress if sharp / worsening pain or new neuro signs). Use this as a coach’s weekly plan to deliver to the client; I kept the layout practical and ready to print.

Quick overview
- Client: 29 y/o recreational climber, right subacromial impingement, 4 months of physio. Cleared for pain‑free ROM only; no overhead loading under load.
- Duration: 12 weeks, 3 phases:
  - Phase 1 Foundations (Weeks 1–4) — build scapular/rotator cuff endurance, movement quality.
  - Phase 2 Build (Weeks 5–8) — increase load, unilateral work, begin very light hang/locking practice.
  - Phase 3 Strength / Transfer & Peak (Weeks 9–12) — high intensity (pulls, hangboard), climbing transfer, taper in Week 12 to peak for trip.
- Frequency: 3 upper sessions/wk (A, B, C), 2 cardio sessions/wk, 1 optional lower/conditioning day midweek, 1 Saturday finisher (full-body fun), daily short mobility micro‑routines and 3 longer mobility sessions/wk.
- Safety rules: pain‑free only; avoid heavy overhead presses; emphasize scapular control and external rotation; use assistance liberally for hangs; consult physio if any concerning symptoms.

Weekly layout example (typical microcycle)
- Mon: Upper Session A (strength focus)
- Tue: Short Cardio (30–40 min) + hangboard/short hang session (from Week 7 onward) + mobility
- Wed: Lower / conditioning or rest + mobility session
- Thu: Upper Session B (mix strength & hangboard)
- Fri: Long Cardio / Endurance (start 45–60 min → progress to 90–150 min) + mobility
- Sat: Upper Session C OR Saturday Finisher (fun full‑body) — depending on energy; finisher ideally after upper session or replace it on lighter weeks
- Sun: Rest / active recovery / short climbing as tolerated

Session templates (used every upper session)
1) Pain check & 4–6 min light cardio warm-up
2) Activation (rotator cuff + scapular): 8–12 min (band ER, prone Y/T/I, scapular pulls)
3) Main strength: 25–35 min (compound horizontal pulls, unilateral rows, landmine presses below shoulder height)
4) Accessory/climb-transfer: 10–15 min (Pallof, carries, isometric lock-offs, hangboard work depending on phase)
5) Mobility / cool-down: 5–10 min (thoracic extension, pec/lat stretches)

Phase 1 — Foundation (Weeks 1–4)
Goals: restore scapular control, rotator cuff endurance, pain‑free ROM, movement patterns.

General programming notes
- Reps high → endurance emphasis for rotator cuff and scapular muscles: 12–20 rep ranges early.
- Main strength work moderate load: 8–12 reps for rows, neutral‑grip presses kept sub‑shoulder.
- Hangboard: not before Week 7. Cardio: 2 sessions/week (short: 30 min zone 2; long: 45–60 min zone 2).

Sample week (Weeks 1–2)
Session A
- Warm-up 5 min bike/row.
- Activation: Banded ER neutral 3×12–15 each; prone T 3×12; scapular pulls 3×8.
- Strength: Chest‑supported DB row 3×10–12; Seated single‑arm cable row 3×10 each.
- Accessory: Pallof press 3×12 each; Farmer carry 3×30–45s.
- Mobility: thoracic foam roll 3–4 min; doorway pec stretch 2×30s.

Session B
- Activation: Banded ER at 30° 3×12; prone Y 3×10.
